what: Reddit runs a network of over 100,000 online communities where users post, discuss and vote on content. It makes money from advertising placed alongside those discussions, and from licensing its archive to AI companies for model training.
customers: Advertisers buying placements, AI companies licensing data, and users, who pay nothing.
money: licensing content to AI companies and user subscriptions
moat: Twenty years of human discussion organised by topic, which cannot be recreated and which has become unusually valuable as training data and as a source search engines surface.
risks: Advertising revenue depends on a small number of large advertisers and on search traffic
Google algorithm changes can swing its user traffic sharply
Moderation is done by volunteers, which creates content and community risk
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 69% last year and about 49% a year over three years
Gross margin of 91% with cash of $3 billion and almost no debt
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Daily active unique visitors and advertising revenue per user.
